messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] production: sustained 429 surge from gpu-hotpath pool (p95 429s > 20%). Queue length rising, autoscaler not adding nodes (hit scale cap). Alerting on-call.
Alice Chen: seeing this in dashboards now, p95 429=27%. Queue growth from 2k -> 12k in 8m.
Bob Martinez: I'm oncall, pinging eng-runtime and eng-sre. Any recent deployments to autoscale/tier-polices?
Carla Nguyen: hi Bob — we rolled a tier-policy change 30m ago that tightened token-bucket burst for dev/prod-guest tiers (lowered burst from 500 -> 100) to reduce noisy neighbor. That might affect routing if requests got misclassified.
Dan O'Leary: autoscaler logs show repeated FailedScaleUp: reached max_instances (pool cap=40). HPA cooldown is default 5m, current members fully saturated.
Eva Singh: support-bot flagged 3 customers seeing 429s and higher latency. Support preparing outbound.
Bob Martinez: action list: 1) quick mitigation to stop customer-facing 429s, 2) restore capacity, 3) rollback risky policy, 4) handoff timeline.
Alice Chen: mitigation attempt 1: increase pool cap to 80 (hotpath pool) — issuing apictl command.
Alice Chen: ```
# increase pool cap
apictl pools update gpu-hotpath --max-instances 80
Result: accepted, new target cap request queued
```
Carla Nguyen: while cap increases, token-bucket enforcement at proxy layer is still dropping bursts. Can we disable strict token enforcement for hotpath-tier?
Dan O'Leary: we can flip the feature flag that enforces token-bucket checks at edge. Doing a temporary toggle now (will revert in 30m).
deploy-bot: deploy started: feature-flag toggle-off token-enforce-hotpath by Dan O'Leary (build 2026.3.412)
deploy-bot: deploy success: toggle-off completed in 18s
Bob Martinez: check metrics after toggle.
Alice Chen: immediate effect: 429 rate dropped from 27% -> 9% in 90s. Queue headcount still growing but slower.
Eva Singh: support: sending initial note to affected customers — informing of degraded availability and we're mitigating.
support-bot: template sent to customers: "We're experiencing elevated 429s for inference requests. We're actively mitigating and will follow up with ETA"
Carla Nguyen: root cause hypothesis: tier policy rollout reduced token-bucket burst for some route-tagging; a small fraction of high-throughput traffic got reclassified into a more constrained policy causing concentrated pressure on limited hotpath pool. Autoscaler hit configured pool cap (40) and cooldown prevented catching up to the incoming delta.
Dan O'Leary: next step: while the pool cap scales, we should rollback the tier policy change to restore previous token-bucket params and avoid aggressive per-client capping.
Alice Chen: initiating rollback of tier policy via infra console now.
Alice Chen: ```
# rollback policy
infractl tiers apply --file=tiers/2026-06-rollback.json
Result: accepted
```
deploy-bot: tiers apply job succeeded (id=job-8732)
Bob Martinez: good. Keep monitoring latency and 429s. If 429s drop < 2% and queue <= 2k, we can de-escalate.
Alice Chen: metrics update: 429s -> 3.2% at 6m post-rollback + toggle-off, queue down to 3.5k. Hotpath pool current instances 42, scaling toward 58.
Eva Singh: support: customers A and B acknowledged, asking for ETA to full recovery. I'll provide rolling updates every 15m.
Carla Nguyen: we should also adjust token-bucket refill rate and burst defaults in config to be more forgiving during autoscale events. Current config: refill=50/s, burst=100. Suggest refill=150/s, burst=500 for production hotpath.
Dan O'Leary: note: autoscaler cooldown meant we couldn't react quickly. Ops action: reduce cooldown from 5m -> 2m for hotpath pools, and increase max_instances temp cap to 120 for the next 2h.
Alice Chen: applying temp overrides: apictl pools update gpu-hotpath --cooldown 120 --max-instances 120
Alice Chen: command accepted.
Bob Martinez: monitoring dashboards. If any regression, we'll roll the toggle and revert caps. Also open postmortem ticket and capture timeline.
Alice Chen: handoff: I'm leaving oncall in 20m. Bob, can you take primary for the next 3h and coordinate with Eng Runtime for post-incident follow-ups? I'll be reachable if needed.
Bob Martinez: taking handoff. I'll own postmortem and customer timeline. Alice, please add your notes to the incident tracker.
Alice Chen: added notes + metric snapshots to incident tracker (incident/2026-06-24-gpu-sat-rlpolicy).
Carla Nguyen: action items captured: 1) revert token-bucket policy rollout permanently until we test with canary traffic, 2) adjust default refill/burst for hotpath, 3) lower autoscaler cooldown + raise temporary cap, 4) add alert for 'pool at cap && queue growing'.
Dan O'Leary: logs snippet (autoscaler): ```
[12:03:12] scale attempt -> desired=58, error: reached max_instances
[12:04:41] scale attempt -> desired=74, error: reached max_instances
[12:07:03] cooldown: nextScaleAllowed at 12:12:03
```
Bob Martinez: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~3 customers affected, degraded success rate from 99.6% -> 72% for 18m window, SLO breach detected, crediting TBD.
Eva Singh: support will collect impacted request IDs and provide a consolidated list to Eng for replay/eval.
support-bot: uploaded customer request logs to shared: /shared/incidents/2026-06-24/gpu-sat-logs.tar.gz
Bob Martinez: resolution timeline: 12:00 ALERT -> 12:09 toggle-off -> 12:14 rollback -> 12:27 queue under control -> 12:40 recovery confirmed. Handoff at 12:45.
Alice Chen: post-incident immediate mitigations implemented: feature-flag toggle-off, tier policy rollback, pool cap increase, cooldown tuning.
Carla Nguyen: long-term mitigation proposals: canary policy rollout, automated rollback if pool cap hits >= 90%, token-bucket simulation in staging with burst traffic, and per-route circuit-breakers that degrade gracefully instead of all-or-nothing 429s.
Bob Martinez: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the postmortem doc and assign owners. Leaving thread open for any late findings.
Eva Singh: thanks — sending final update to customers now. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.
